diagrams.title: One Evidence Desk, Three Distinct Recovery Lanes
diagrams.subtitle: Classify first; verify eligibility before assigning collectible value.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Drawback, tariff refunds, and antitrust distributions are alternative routes through this workflow, not sequential recoveries on the same dollars. Importer duty principal, merchant purchase volume, and gross settlement pools never become operator revenue. Formal customs filings use a licensed 19 CFR Part 111 customs broker or trade counsel with valid Customs Powers of Attorney.
diagrams.caption: The operator sells evidence assembly and recovery coordination; only earned contingency fees enter the revenue scorecard.

stages.label: Authorize the account
stages.detail: Execute the recovery agreement, identify the claimant entity, document record-access authority, and price a zero-upfront 25%–35% contingency on realized recoveries. Obtain the required Customs Power of Attorney directly for the filing professional.

stages.label: Route the recovery
stages.detail: Create distinct ledgers for 19 U.S.C. § 1313 drawback, 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests or ACE Post-Summary Correction, and existing B2B antitrust settlements. Assign each ledger its own deadline, collectible base, cost budget, and cash estimate.

stages.label: Reconcile primary evidence
stages.detail: Use ImportGenius or Panjiva for discovery, then reconcile authorized ACE CBP Form 7501 records, duty payments, export bills of lading, and inventory movements. For settlements, reconcile accounts-payable or processor records to class periods. Manifest matches and eight-digit HTS matches are candidate links, not proof of statutory eligibility.

stages.label: Submit the correct packet
stages.detail: The broker or trade counsel files the correct customs route and retains Part 190 evidence for drawback. Settlement packets follow the court-approved claim form, allocation plan, third-party filer rules, and claimant authorization. Block duplicate claims and unsupported substitutions before submission.

stages.label: Reconcile cash and fee
stages.detail: Match the agency refund or administrator distribution to the claimant ledger, resolve offsets and reversals, and calculate the contracted earned fee. Record client recovery principal separately from operator consideration; retain an auditable bridge from payment notice to fee invoice.

diagrams.title: From 240 Screened Accounts to 20 Paid Accounts
diagrams.subtitle: Illustrative mature annual cohort supporting $515,000 in earned fees.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Every stage is a subset of the preceding account cohort, with one primary lane assigned per account to avoid double counting. Counts are planning assumptions, not observed conversion rates. Twenty paid accounts comprise ten drawback accounts, six tariff-refund accounts, and four settlement accounts. At an illustrative 30% fee, recoveries of $1,000,000, $500,000, and $216,666.67 produce $300,000, $150,000, and $65,000 in fees after cent rounding. Remaining submitted accounts are still pending, deficient, or unpaid at the measurement date.
diagrams.caption: The cohort converts 8.33% of screened accounts into paid accounts; average earned fees are $25,750 per paid account.

stages.label: Screened accounts
stages.detail: Identify importer-exporter pairs, documented entry-error candidates, and businesses potentially inside an existing settlement class. Count businesses once, rather than counting each entry, shipment, or purchase as a separate prospect.

stages.label: Authorized evidence access
stages.detail: Obtain written authority and usable source records from 120 of the 240 screened accounts. Exclude businesses whose records cannot be accessed through authorized channels or whose contracting entity cannot establish ownership.

stages.label: Eligibility substantiated
stages.detail: Validate deadlines, claimant identity, statutory route, recoverable duty components, or settlement class membership. Remove prohibited duties, expired remedies, unsupported exports, and purchases outside the court-defined class period.

stages.label: Complete packets submitted
stages.detail: Submit forty complete account packets through the required filing channel. Record submission acknowledgments and track all agency or administrator requests without treating submitted claim amounts as earned fee revenue.

stages.label: Cash realized and fees earned
stages.detail: Recognize $515,000 in earned operator fees from paid recoveries, not from requested awards. Ten drawback accounts average $30,000 in fees, six refund accounts average $25,000, and four settlement accounts average $16,250.

diagrams.title: $515,000 Earned Fees to $231,750 Owner Profit
diagrams.subtitle: Six bars reconcile the Formula v2.0 Base-Case 45.0% net margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The first bar is gross operator fee revenue, the next four are negative expense movements, and the final bar is an absolute ending total rather than an additional movement. All figures are annual USD. The operator earns its own contracted fees; client recovery principal is excluded rather than grossed up and reduced by a retained-share factor. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent assessment still applies to third-party consideration. Owner profit is after the modeled business expenses, before owner personal taxes, with no extra owner salary deducted. Contractor fees plus evidence costs are variable delivery costs; technology plus overhead are recurring operating costs.

stages.label: Earned operator fees
stages.detail: The illustrative lane mix contributes $300,000 from drawback, $150,000 from tariff refunds, and $65,000 from settlement distributions. Approximately $1.717 million in client recoveries supports these fees at 30%; that recovery principal is excluded.

stages.label: Contractor delivery expense
stages.detail: Budget the three core contractors collectively: licensed broker, evidence analyst, and trade or settlement counsel. Their compensation is an operator expense, not a second claim against the client's recovered principal.

stages.label: Evidence acquisition expense
stages.detail: Budget purchased records, scanning, retrieval, and secure document delivery separately from contractor labor. Paid accounts consume $24,600 under lane budgets; another $11,400 covers screened, unresolved, and unsuccessful account evidence.

stages.label: Technology and subscriptions
stages.detail: Cover manifest intelligence, authorized record reconciliation, secure storage, accounting, and document workflow software. Do not assume public manifests replace private entry evidence or provide unrestricted ACE account access.

stages.label: Insurance and operating overhead
stages.detail: Cover insurance, accounting, prospecting, routine administration, and modest bond-related expense where contracted. Together with technology, recurring costs total $73,250 annually, or $6,104.17 monthly, inside the $1,500–$9,500 planning range.

stages.label: Owner operating profit
stages.detail: Total annual expenses equal $283,250. Conservative economics remain $110,000 revenue, $74,800 expenses, and $35,200 profit at 32%; scaled economics remain $920,000 revenue, $386,400 expenses, and $533,600 profit at 58%.

diagrams.title: Five Fee Yields on the Same $100,000 Recovery
diagrams.subtitle: Compare earned operator fees, not import value or settlement pool size.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each independent bar assumes $100,000 of realized eligible client recovery and a stated illustrative contingency within 25%–35%. Bars show revenue before delivery costs, not net profit, expected claim value, or additive annual forecasts. Drawback recovery is calculated after applicable statutory limits, often 99% of qualifying duties, taxes, and fees; $100,000 here is the actual recovery base. Fee terms require client acceptance and must fit the applicable filing arrangement and any settlement-specific restrictions.
diagrams.caption: Higher headline percentages do not offset weak evidence, delayed cash, duplicate claims, or nonrecoverable duty components.

stages.label: Direct unused-merchandise drawback
stages.detail: Use a substantiated 19 U.S.C. § 1313(j)(1) claim with qualifying unused merchandise and timely export or destruction. Specific identification and clean inventory tracing support the lower illustrative service rate.

stages.label: Substitution drawback
stages.detail: Use a qualifying 19 U.S.C. § 1313(j)(2) route with the applicable eight-digit HTS classification test, possession requirements, special classification restrictions, and valuation limits. Identical tariff codes alone do not establish eligibility.

stages.label: ACE entry correction refund
stages.detail: Correct an eligible unliquidated entry through ACE Post-Summary Correction using documented classification, valuation, or origin facts. The filing professional verifies current CBP timing rules and entry-type restrictions before preparing the correction.

stages.label: Timely liquidation protest
stages.detail: Use 19 U.S.C. § 1514 and 19 CFR Part 174 for a protestable decision filed within the applicable deadline. The collectible base is the supported refund actually paid, not the full duties shown on every challenged entry.

stages.label: B2B settlement distribution
stages.detail: Package eligible purchase or interchange records for an existing court-approved settlement. Apply the fee only to the client's realized distribution under accepted terms, with required filer disclosures and direct-filing information.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Valuing a Claim
diagrams.subtitle: Test the selected lane, then apply the shared authority and cash check.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The first three nodes are alternative lane branches; an eligible branch proceeds to the fourth shared check. A failed eligibility test stops that lane unless a documented correction remains possible. Documentation budgets are incremental purchased-evidence costs per paid account and exclude contractor labor. Cash windows are illustrative planning intervals from a complete filing to receipt, not agency or administrator service commitments.
diagrams.caption: Separate eligibility, collectible base, evidence expense, surety exposure, and payment timing before assigning expected fee value.

stages.label: Drawback eligibility
stages.value: If eligible, continue to shared check
stages.detail: Apply 19 U.S.C. § 1313 and 19 CFR Part 190, including the applicable export or destruction requirements and generally the five-year claim-completion limit measured from importation. Exclude duties barred from drawback, including antidumping and countervailing duties. Base value on qualifying refundable duty components after statutory limits. Budget $1,500 in evidence cost per paid account. Accelerated payment requires applicable CBP authorization and bond coverage; without it, plan standard payment. Model 6–18 months for standard recovery, potentially longer.

stages.label: Tariff-refund route
stages.detail: Use PSC only for eligible unliquidated entries, ordinarily within 300 days of entry and at least 15 days before scheduled liquidation, whichever deadline arrives first. Use 19 U.S.C. § 1514 protests generally within 180 days of liquidation or the applicable protestable decision. Base value on substantiated overpaid duties. Budget $1,200 per paid account. An ordinary refund request has no drawback accelerated-payment bond, although existing entry bonds remain separate. Model 3–12 months after a complete filing, potentially longer.

stages.label: Settlement class eligibility
stages.detail: Use the settlement order, claim deadline, class period, allocation plan, and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23. Check claimant identity, exclusions, releases, assignments, and duplicate submissions. The collectible base is the eventual allocated distribution, not purchase volume or the settlement fund. Budget $600 per paid account. Ordinary administrative claim filing generally requires no customs surety bond; inspect the actual order for separate security terms. Model 6–24 months or longer, especially when appeals delay distribution.

stages.label: Authority and cash capacity
stages.detail: Verify broker or trade-counsel authority and valid Customs Powers of Attorney for formal CBP filings, Part 190 records for drawback, and court-required third-party filer disclosures for settlements explaining direct filing at zero cost. Confirm surety capacity before requesting accelerated payment. If collateral exceeds available capital, use the standard-payment route or defer the account; never fund operations from client principal.

diagrams.title: Four Core People; Six at Scaled Capacity
diagrams.subtitle: Base pod: 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled pod: 2 FT + 4 C.
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time operator; C means contracted specialist. The first four seats form the Conservative and Base pod. The final two seats are added only for the Scaled scenario. Counsel must possess the competence required by the accepted case mix; narrow the service scope if the retained professional cannot cover it. Software and licensed data subscriptions are tools, not additional seats.
diagrams.caption: Conservative revenue and profit are $110,000 and $35,200; Base figures are $515,000 and $231,750; Scaled figures are $920,000 and $533,600 with six people.

stages.label: Owner and recovery lead
stages.detail: Own client acquisition, contract economics, lane assignment, cash forecasting, fee reconciliation, and account-level exception decisions. Maintain separation between operator consideration and funds belonging to the claimant.

stages.label: Licensed customs broker
stages.detail: Execute authorized customs business under 19 CFR Part 111. Validate drawback routes, PSC availability, protest submissions, POA scope, and bond arrangements while preserving filing acknowledgments and supporting records.

stages.label: Evidence reconciliation analyst
stages.detail: Match ACE entry lines to source invoices, inventory events, and export bills of lading. Assemble settlement purchase evidence, track reconciliation exceptions, and maintain the duplicate-claim ledger across all three lanes.

stages.label: Trade and settlement counsel
stages.detail: Resolve complex statutory eligibility, protest grounds, settlement-class interpretation, and filer-disclosure requirements. Escalate disputes beyond the contracted scope rather than letting administrative staff make unsupported legal determinations.

stages.label: Operations and collections lead
stages.detail: Take over deadline monitoring, evidence-request scheduling, status reconciliation, invoice collections, and operating capacity planning. Add this seat against demonstrated workload and collected fee capacity.

stages.label: Settlement ledger specialist
stages.detail: Reconcile high-volume accounts-payable and processor exports, normalize class-period purchases, resolve entity mapping, and package administrator responses without substituting purchase totals for distributable recovery estimates.

diagrams.title: Allocate $8,000–$35,000 Without Buying Claim Principal
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets; illustrative Base launch allocation totals $20,000.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values encode the $20,000 Base launch plan. Each bucket also states a lean and expanded allocation; lean allocations sum to $8,000 and expanded allocations sum to $35,000. These are startup capital allocations, not annual revenue scenarios or additional waterfall expenses. Reconcile actual spending to the expense ledger to avoid counting the same cost twice. Substantial surety collateral is outside these budgets; choose standard payment if accelerated payment cannot fit verified capital capacity.
diagrams.caption: Lean: $1,000 + $2,000 + $3,000 + $2,000 = $8,000. Base launch: $20,000. Expanded: $4,000 + $9,000 + $14,000 + $8,000 = $35,000.

stages.label: Entity and risk setup
stages.detail: Fund entity setup, contract preparation, insurance deposits, and authority documentation. Keep client recovery agreements separate from broker Powers of Attorney and settlement administrator authorization forms.

stages.label: Secure evidence tooling
stages.detail: Fund initial manifest intelligence, encrypted storage, reconciliation scripts, access controls, and audit logging. Purchase only the data coverage needed for the first authorized cohort instead of broad speculative datasets.

stages.label: Specialist launch capacity
stages.detail: Reserve broker, analyst, and counsel capacity for initial eligibility work and sample packets. Obtain written scopes and fee schedules before accepting labor-intensive cases with uncertain records or fragile deadlines.

stages.label: Working-capital reserve
stages.detail: Hold cash for evidence retrieval, recurring overhead, and collection delays. At $1,500 monthly spend, the Base reserve covers three months; at $9,500, less than one month. Throttle intake when expected payment timing exceeds runway.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to a Controlled Recovery Desk
diagrams.subtitle: Build evidence and filing readiness before forecasting near-term cash.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Four weekly milestones cover Days 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, and 22–30. The canonical first-deal planning range is 1–3 months; a signed engagement is distinct from a paid agency refund or settlement distribution. The first month targets authorized evidence, tested reconciliation, and complete packets, not collection of the annual Base revenue target.
diagrams.caption: Launch with a small, traceable cohort and preserve the right to decline defective evidence before spending scarce specialist capacity.

stages.label: Days 1–7
stages.value: Define lanes and appoint the core pod
stages.detail: Contract the broker, analyst, and counsel; establish 25%–35% fee terms; configure separate recovery and revenue ledgers. Build statutory deadline fields, claimant identity checks, and court-specific disclosure templates. Allocate startup capital without assuming accelerated-payment access.

stages.label: Days 8–14
stages.detail: Obtain source records from three pilot accounts, ideally one per lane. Reconcile a sample entry-to-export chain, a correction or protest candidate, and an existing settlement purchase ledger. Record actual evidence gaps and retrieval costs.

stages.label: Days 15–21
stages.detail: Have the filing professional verify customs eligibility and clocks; have counsel verify settlement class and filer terms. Test duplicate detection, duty-component exclusions, export trace completeness, and fee calculations against source documents before valuing the pilot pipeline.

stages.label: Days 22–30
stages.value: Submit complete pilots and set cadence
stages.detail: Submit only complete, authorized packets through the appropriate channel and capture acknowledgments. Set weekly exception triage, monthly cash forecasts, and account-level cost tracking. Carry pending claims as pipeline records, not realized recovery or earned operator fees.
